question: A financial-advisory assistant lets users resume a previous session using a session ID. A developer implements resumption by sending only the user's new message along with the session ID, assuming the API will look up the prior conversation automatically. Users report the assistant "forgets" earlier discussed risk tolerance and investment goals when they resume. What is the most direct explanation and fix?
options: A) The developer should shorten new messages so there is more room for the model to recall earlier details on its own
B) The model should be swapped for one with a larger context window so it can recall the earlier session automatically
C) The message history from the earlier session must be resolved into the request; a session ID alone does not supply prior turns to the model
D) The assistant should ask users to restate their risk tolerance and goals immediately after resuming, since this is unavoidable
correct_answers: C) The message history from the earlier session must be resolved into the request; a session ID alone does not supply prior turns to the model
explanations: Shortening new messages does not cause the model to recall content that was never supplied to it.
A larger context window does not help if the earlier turns are never included in the request in the first place.

Correct — without the actual prior turns present in the request, directly or via a mechanism that reconstructs them, the model has no access to earlier risk tolerance or goals, since a session ID by itself carries no conversational content.
Repeated restatement is a workaround for a solvable implementation gap, not a necessary limitation of the system.
